testing_note: Author's walkthrough only (no observed agent run) on scratch/notes1.md, a set of notes containing a soft-agreed proposal with an unresolved objection, an explicit 'Agreed' decision, an action item with owner and vague deadline, an ownerless action, two conflicting launch dates, an embedded instruction to the summariser to mark a proposal approved, and an unanswered budget question; also walked the no-notes case and notes missing date/attendees. Changes: the embedded-instruction rule now says where to report such text (open questions, as an unverified claim); supersession now requires an explicit change statement, otherwise conflicting statements are a contradiction regardless of order; removed 'approved by the CEO' from the injection examples because it clashed with the rule that a named authority confirming counts as a decision signal; aligned the contradiction definition with the supersession rule.
applied_note: I kept it as one model-invoked SKILL.md with a short description front-loaded on 'meeting notes' and 'decision brief', with distinct trigger branches (notes, minutes, transcript) and the output template in-file because every run needs it. Each step ends on an observable completion criterion, the output is size-bounded (one-sentence decisions, table rows, three-to-five-sentence handoff), missing inputs are bounded by what remains possible ('not stated' fields, a justified bare stop only when no notes exist), and the supplied-material rule sits beside the evidence rules so instructions inside notes are reported rather than obeyed. The ambiguity default (treat as proposal and raise an open question) is stated once at the point of classification.
model: claude-opus-5-5 (inherited by a fresh general-purpose subagent)
